messages:
alex_support: FYI we just got an escalation from Acme (tenant acme-inc). After yesterday's rollout they see the same user session get conflicting product info across requests. They say sometimes the model answers that feature X is supported and on the next call says it's not. Can someone look into routing/fallback changes around the rollout? :eyes:

maria_oncall: Noted. Do they have a session_id we can repro with? Also what model variants are in their route?

alex_support: Customer provided a few request ids and this minimal repro flow: they call chat API with same session_id, same system prompt and two near-identical user messages. Sometimes response A (variant-v1) then later response B (variant-v2). They attached a couple of request payloads.

jon_eng: Can you paste the exact payload and request ids here? If we can repro locally we can check routing logs. Sounds like a sticky session isn't being honored or fallback order changed.

alex_support: Paste of one payload (sanitized):
```json
{"tenant":"acme-inc","session_id":"s-3fa9","model":"redwood-chat","prompt":"Is feature X available?","temperature":0.0}
```
Request ids: r-8901, r-8904 (these map to the same session).

sophia_ml: Quick hypothesis: we had a canary that introduced a fallback-to-quantized-variant on load that might not preserve deterministic outputs. If routing switched between variant-a (fp16) and variant-b (int8-q4) mid-session, outputs could diverge.

infra-bot: Routing policy change deployed by deploy/route-fallback-2026-03-14 at 21:12 UTC. Affected services: routing-service v2.1.3.

maria_oncall: Thanks infra-bot. jon, could you grep routing logs for session s-3fa9 around the request ids? Check for route decisions and whether stickiness cookie was present.

jon_eng: I pulled logs. For r-8901 routing-service chose variant-a on node gpunode-12. For r-8904 it selected variant-b on gpunode-21. There is a short 5s gap; the session cookie was present in both requests. However, the routing decision included a fallback flag due to node throttling on variant-a at r-8904 time. So it intentionally rerouted.

alex_support: Customer says reroute happened inside a single conversation, they want consistent answers. We need to propose mitigation and communicate.

sophia_ml: Short term: suggest enabling tenant-level model pinning so acme-inc stays on variant-a. Also enable response metadata to include model_variant and model_fingerprint so customer and support can trace. Medium term: we should ensure variant family compatibility for semantic parity when falling back (same tokenizer, same seed policies).

jon_eng: Added a temporary tenant pin: PUT /tenants/acme-inc/config {"pinned_model":"variant-a"} and rolled back the routing fallback for that tenant. Also flagged that routing-service change which allowed fallback-to-quantized without parity checks.

maria_oncall: Can support confirm with customer after pinning and rollback? Also collect a clean repro after pin to validate issue resolved.

alex_support: Replied to customer: pinned them to variant-a and asked them to run the same sequence. Asked for a fresh request id. They responded r-8912 and said outputs are now consistent. :thumbsup:

jon_eng: Follow-ups for backlog: (1) add a parity-check validation when promoting fallback variants, (2) telemetry: include model_variant in API responses, (3) routing: prefer capacity-shed before cross-variant fallback for sticky sessions. I'll create tickets.

sophia_ml: Also will run an evaluation comparing variant-a vs variant-b on the customer's prompt suite to quantify semantic drift and add to Optimize recommendations.

alex_support: Closing loop: customer is satisfied for now, asked for ETA on a permanent fix. We'll keep them updated. Marking as resolved externally but retaining internal follow-up items. :white_check_mark:
